title: Thermal buffer weight-shepherd and KV conditioner for SLA stability
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce a coordinated prewarm strategy that smooths weight loading across nodes (thermal buffer / weight-shepherd) and runs deterministic KV conditioning passes (KV conditioner) prior to routing live traffic. Objective: reduce 99th percentile cold-start latency spikes during burst attach and protect throughput guarantees for Dedicated customers without excessive GPU residency costs.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end test that simulates tenant burst attach and shows 95% reduction in 99p cold-start latency spikes compared to baseline
Autoscaler and fleet-controller can apply thermal buffer policy to pause aggressive attach when average node load would breach configured SLA headroom
KV conditioner completes prefix/KV priming for model variants within a target window (configurable, default 120s) and reports priming health to Console
Cost impact: additional steady-state memory residency increases < 2% for tenants using the policy compared to baseline warm-pool reservation
Operational visibility: Console dashboard shows per-tenant warm score, KV primer progress, and 'shepherd' activity with trace links to serving nodes
notes: 2025-01-16 - Aisha: Kickoff meeting. Agreed scope: two complementary subsystems: Weight Shepherd (staged weight ingestion + staged residency) and KV Conditioner (deterministic prefix walks + lightweight token replay).

2025-01-20 - Liam: Spike completed. Prototype implemented that staggers weight mmap across 8 sequential micro-batches; observed reduced IO saturation on NVMe but higher short-lived memory pressure. See spike PR #1189.

2025-01-28 - SRE review: Concern about scheduler jitter when many tenants use policy simultaneously. Decided to gate activation with cluster-wide admission token and to expose a max-concurrent-shepherds flag per-region.
2025-02-05 - Design review (Vera): Console UI wireframes accepted. Need a warm-score telemetry schema that ties into rollout and refund rules for Dedicated customers.

2025-02-11 - Performance bench: With staged ingestion (shepherd) + KV conditioner (deterministic prefix of 4 token steps) we see 40-60% fewer cold-start tokens served from disk during first 30s of attach in synthetic tenant replay tests.

2025-02-18 - Implementation note: Using existing KV worker pool but adding a low-priority lane for conditioners to avoid contention with live requests. Requires small changes to worker admission and the tracing tags for primer runs.
